## The argument in one minute

Characteristics can describe overlapping stock exposures. The Gram matrix of the characteristic panel gives a direct way to measure their scale and overlap. Its use as a normalisation rule changes loading units, and a fixed numerical factor ridge can then change the portfolio's exposure penalty even when forecasts nearly agree. A controlled re-solve removes that ridge and nearly eliminates the holdings gap. A separate within-fit experiment shows that restoring the retained intercept mean explains most of a historical gross-performance increment. The paper distinguishes geometry, portfolio penalties, and mean usage rather than merging them into a claim of universal superiority.

## Reproducibility

The research release bundles the manuscript, slides, and a standalone replication that recalculates portfolio statistics, paired block-bootstrap inference, input ablations, and rolling characteristic geometry from bundled monthly inputs. The original stock panel is not redistributed.
